tagline: Three mountains and hundreds of turns, Marion to Tazewell.
intro: North of Marion, Route 16 passes the west shore of Hungry Mother Lake and sets out on the 32 miles to Tazewell known as the Back of the Dragon. Larry Brent Davidson pushed for the name because the road put him in mind of the humps on a dragon's back.

It crosses Walker Mountain, the North Fork of the Holston at Chatham Hill, then Brushy and Clinch mountains. The limit is generally 55, and many of the curves are posted at 15. The designated byway begins farther south, at Dickey Gap above Sugar Grove, and runs on to Pisgah; the line drawn here keeps to Marion and Tazewell.

moments.title: Hungry Mother State Park
moments.text: The name comes from a legend in which Molly Marley and her small child escaped raiders, and the child, finding help alone, could say only "Hungry Mother."

moments.title: Thompson Valley
moments.text: Off Clinch Mountain a single hairpin drops the road into the wide Thompson Valley, where the community is named for William and Archibald Thompson, its first settlers in the early 19th century.

moments.title: Tazewell
moments.text: Called Jeffersonville until 1892, the town is said to be one of the smallest in the country ever to run a streetcar, a five-cent trolley that quit in 1933.
